title: Five event-store test cases have no coverage at unit or integration level (TC-ES-01-02/03/04, TC-ES-05-04, TC-ES-07-02)
notes:
Discovered while resolving ISS-0148 (GH #464), which replaced 25 SkipZigTest stubs in tests/unit/event_store_test.zig with real assertions. Of the 25 stubs, 15 already had named integration counterparts and 9 became real unit tests. These 5 had NEITHER, so removing the stub would have silently dropped the requirement's only trace. Each asserts a property of persisted state and so belongs in tests/integration/event_store_integration_test.zig:
  TC-ES-01-02 append to non-existent instance -> InstanceNotFound (ES-01, HTTP 404)
  TC-ES-01-03 append to COMPLETED instance -> InstanceTerminated (ES-01, HTTP 409)
  TC-ES-01-04 append to CANCELLED instance -> InstanceTerminated (ES-01, HTTP 409)
  TC-ES-05-04 registerType duplicate name+version -> DuplicateEventTypeVersion (ES-05, HTTP 409)
  TC-ES-07-02 archive returns count of moved rows (ES-07)
The production code paths for all five exist in src/event_store/; only the tests are missing.
candidate_resolution: Add five integration tests to tests/integration/event_store_integration_test.zig following the existing per-test-UUID fixture pattern in that file. TC-ES-01-03/04 need an instance_projections row seeded with status COMPLETED/CANCELLED. TC-ES-05-04 needs two registerType calls with the same (name, schema_version). TC-ES-07-02 needs the archive() return value asserted against a known row count.
resolution: Added five real integration tests to tests/integration/event_store_integration_test.zig, all executing against real PostgreSQL via BPM_TEST_DB_URL (no mocks/stubs, DIRECTIVE T-1): TC-ES-01-02 (append to an instance absent from instance_projections -> StoreError.InstanceNotFound, ES-01 HTTP 404), TC-ES-01-03 (instance seeded status=COMPLETED -> StoreError.InstanceTerminated, ES-01 HTTP 409), TC-ES-01-04 (status=CANCELLED -> InstanceTerminated, ES-01 HTTP 409, plus an ACTIVE control append that must succeed), TC-ES-05-04 (two registerType calls with identical name+schema_version -> RegistryError.DuplicateEventTypeVersion, ES-05 HTTP 409, plus a version-2 control proving the key is (name, version) not name alone), TC-ES-07-02 (five appended events, three backdated 10 days past a keep_days=1 policy -> archive() moves exactly those three and leaves the two non-expired ones). All three ES-01/ES-05 cases register their event type first, because Store.append() runs ES-05 registry validation BEFORE the instance lookup — without that the calls would fail with UnknownEventType and never reach the code path under test. TC-ES-07-02 exposed a REAL PRODUCTION DEFECT: Store.archive() in src/event_store/store.zig returned the number of retention POLICIES it applied (total_moved += 1 per branch, with the stale comment 'real count from DELETE RETURNING not available yet'), not the number of rows moved — so it returned 1 where ES-07 and tests/specs/ES-01-08.md require 3. Fixed per Unblock-Everything by converting all five DELETE statements (keep_days, hard_delete_days, keep_count, hard_delete_count, and the global-fallback sweep) from conn.exec to conn.query with RETURNING event_id, accumulating rows.len. No caller broke: every archive() caller discards the value. Mutation-verified: reverting the keep_days branch to total_moved += 1 makes TC-ES-07-02 fail with 'expected 3, found 1'; each of the other four tests was likewise mutated (wrong expected error, ACTIVE instead of COMPLETED/CANCELLED, version 7 instead of duplicate version 1) and each failed, then all were restored.
prevention: The five cases existed only as error.SkipZigTest stubs, which Zig counts as passes — the file reported green for months while three MUST acceptance criteria (ES-01's two HTTP-409 paths and ES-05's HTTP-409 duplicate path) had no executing assertion at any level, and the archive() row-count defect sat undetected behind the one stub that would have caught it. A skipped test is absence of coverage, not coverage: tools/lint_test_isolation.py already flags error.SkipZigTest on MUST tests, and TEST-DESIGNER is required to run it before handoff. All five new tests use per-test UUID fixtures via TestHarness.newUuidString and a uniqueName() helper for event type names and idempotency keys, so nothing collides with a sibling test binary on the shared database — TC-ES-07-02 in particular needs a unique event type because archive() is driven by a per-event_type policy and a shared name would let concurrent tests archive each other's rows. Also note the stale-comment smell: 'real count from DELETE RETURNING not available yet' outlived the limitation it described (Conn.query has always supported RETURNING); such comments should be re-checked against the current API rather than trusted.
